topic: What if you never needed to sleep?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
SKIP SLEEP FOREVER?

power.rule: you never get tired, every night is free time
power.look: the bedroom clock spins forward, a SKIP chip, the bed stays made; Pip's eyes snap wide open with a cool flash

script.text: Midnight. One more level. Skip sleep. You win.
Three a.m. Big test tomorrow. Skip sleep. You read the whole book.
Your friend sleeps over. He's out cold. Skip sleep. You just... watch him. All night.
What if you could skip sleep forever?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch: when you sleep, the gaps between your brain cells open up by sixty percent, to wash out waste. That's real.
So if you never sleep... where's it all going?

science.claim: When you sleep, the gaps between your brain cells open up by sixty percent, to wash out waste.
science.working: In sleeping (and anaesthetised) mice the interstitial space volume fraction rose from about 14% awake to about 23% asleep, a 60% increase, and the faster interstitial flow cleared beta-amyloid about twice as fast. The study is in mice; the script says 'your brain' as the genre does, the schematic labels it a sleep study.
science.source: Xie et al., 'Sleep drives metabolite clearance from the adult brain', Science 342 (2013) 373-377

science.working: Adults are recommended 7 or more hours a night; 8 is the round figure for a full night.
science.source: Watson et al., AASM/SRS consensus, Sleep 38 (2015) 843-844

Pip sits up in bed, laptop on his knees, screen light on his face; heavy, tired lids
SKIP: Pip's tired eyes snap wide open, cyan glint, flash
Pip throws both arms up in bed, the laptop glowing; the whole room lit by the lamp
the clock reads 03:00, the calendar soft behind
Pip at the desk under the lamp, a tower of books, slumping, tired
SKIP: eyes snap open, glint; he sits bolt upright
the open book's pages flip by in a blur, finished books stacking beside it
Mo has the bed, sitting up asleep against the pillows; Pip on the beanbag with the laptop
Mo out cold, head lolling, eyes shut, the lamp warm on him
SKIP: Pip's eyes wide in the dark, glinting, unblinking
Pip's dark head in the foreground, Mo asleep beyond; the clock races 01:00 to 06:00
the premise over the city at sunrise; Pip on the roof, wide awake
Pip stretches, happy; a +8 HOURS label floats up
Pip tries to shut his eyes; the lids drop and snap back open, he can't
two brain cells, the gap between them widens: AWAKE 14% to ASLEEP 23%, +60% counting up
waste specks wash out through the widened gap
Pip, worried; the light turning red
night again: the lamp flickers and dies, the clock reads 04:12, only Pip's glinting eyes in the dark
